extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying creative short story generation, evaluation of LLMs, and computational creativity
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating short stories produced by humans and large language models using automated metrics and human (expert and non-expert) ratings on a five-sentence cue-word writing task; includes Turing Test judgments and cross-model/human comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: One of several dimensions of creativity measured automatically; used to compare model- and human-generated stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract notes automated metrics show LLMs tend to fall short in terms of novelty when compared to average human writers; treat novelty as a distinct axis of creative quality alongside surprise, diversity, and linguistic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: A measured dimension of creativity (referred to as 'surprise') used in automated evaluation of stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors report LLMs underperform relative to humans on surprise; include surprise as an explicit metric capturing unexpected or non-obvious story elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated measure of the diversity of generated stories across outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity is used to assess variety in content/style; abstract reports LLMs fall short in diversity compared to average human writers, so evaluation should measure intra-model and cross-author diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic complexity (stylistic complexity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of linguistic or stylistic complexity of stories; automated metrics indicate LLMs generate stylistically complex stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract emphasizes that LLMs produce high stylistic/linguistic complexity even when they lag on novelty and surprise — include syntactic/lexical complexity and stylistic markers as separate evaluative signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated multi-dimensional evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of automated metrics to evaluate stories across several creativity-related dimensions (novelty, surprise, diversity, linguistic complexity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study applies automated measures across multiple axes; evaluations should report per-axis scores and consider how automated signals correspond with human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human creativity ratings (expert and non-expert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting creativity ratings from non-expert and expert human raters to judge how creative stories are perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract notes expert ratings generally coincide with automated metrics, while non-experts may rate LLM stories as more creative than human-generated ones — record rater expertise and analyze rater-model interaction and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turing Test classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting Turing Test-style judgments (classifications of stories as human- or model-generated) from human raters and LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Turing-style classification as an evaluative measure of human-likeness; compare these classifications with creativity ratings and automated metrics to understand perceived origin and creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-sentence cue-word-based creative story-writing task
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific generation task used: a five-sentence, cue-word-based creative story-writing prompt used for both humans and LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task design imposes a structural constraint (five sentences) and uses cue words — evaluations must account for prompt/task constraints when comparing creativity across sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-population comparative design (60 LLMs vs 60 people)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation conducted across a large set of models and human participants (60 LLMs and 60 people) for comparative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors use broad sampling of models and people; as a rubric point, evaluations should sample sufficiently many models and human writers to support generalizable comparisons and report sample composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater-model discordance and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed differences in ratings: expert ratings align with automated metrics, but LLMs and non-experts tend to rate LLM-produced stories as more creative than human-produced ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting creativity judgments, account for systematic differences by rater type (expert vs non-expert vs LLM), and analyze reasons for discordance (e.g., stylistic cues that inflate perceived creativity).
